issues.legal_issue: A claim for compensation for land erosion cannot succeed when concurrent factual findings attribute the erosion to natural causes and the evidence does not connect it to government action.
material_facts: The land had been requisitioned, and the claimant alleged that a portion had eroded because of government action.
A bridge had been constructed over part of a nearby river after requisition, but there was no evidence that its construction caused the erosion.
The District Court and High Court both found that the erosion was due to natural causes.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to disturb the concurrent findings and rejected the claim based on the alleged erosion.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no basis to overturn concurrent factual findings where the evidence did not establish that government action caused the alleged damage.

predicates.erosion_compensation_appeal: An appeal concerns a claim for compensation for erosion of land after it was taken into government possession.
predicates.concurrent_findings_against_causation: The lower courts both found that the erosion was not caused by government action.
predicates.evidence_connecting_government_action_to: Evidence connects an act or omission of the government to the erosion.

issues.definition: When an erosion-compensation appeal challenges concurrent findings against government causation and no evidence connects government action to the erosion, the challenge is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for land used for roads and canals is limited to the expenditure necessary to restore it to its condition when it was taken, rather than compensation as if the land had been acquired.
material_facts: A portion of the requisitioned land was covered by roads and canals.
The claimant argued that the land was a total loss because it could not be returned to its original use.
The High Court concluded that the claim should be limited to the amount needed to put the land in the condition it was in when requisitioned.
The District Court had awarded compensation for that portion as if it had been acquired.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the limitation of compensation to the cost of restoring the land and rejected compensation for the land as though it had been acquired.
issues.legal_principle: For land requisitioned and later used for roads or canals, the Court accepted restoration expenditure as the measure of the claim, rather than treating the land as acquired.

predicates.requisition_compensation_appeal: An appeal concerns compensation for land that was requisitioned for public use.
predicates.land_used_for_roads_or_canals: The requisitioned land was used for roads or canals.
predicates.restoration_to_prior_condition_is_the_co: The evidence supports measuring the compensation by the expenditure needed to restore the land to its condition when taken.

issues.definition: In a requisition-compensation appeal involving land used for roads or canals, when restoration expenditure is the applicable measure, compensation is limited to restoration cost.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation valuation is not displaced by higher-priced transactions that are fictitious or do not provide comparable evidence of the value of the land in question.
material_facts: The claimant challenged compensation of Rs. 300 per bigha by relying on sales said to show prices as high as Rs. 2,000 per bigha.
One of the higher-priced sales was made by the claimant, and the High Court found it fictitious.
Other relied-on sales concerned land in a distant adjoining village and land affected by increased building activity.
The Supreme Court agreed that the cited sales were not comparable instances.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge to the compensation valuation based on the cited higher-priced sales.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirement that relied-on sale transactions be genuine and comparable to the land being valued; the cited transactions did not meet that basis for comparison.

predicates.compensation_valuation_appeal: An appeal challenges the amount of compensation fixed for land.
predicates.higher_priced_sales_relied_on: The claimant relies on higher-priced sales to support a higher valuation.
predicates.relied_on_sales_not_genuine_or_comparabl: The relied-on sales are fictitious or differ materially in location or circumstances from the land being valued.

issues.definition: When a compensation-valuation appeal relies on higher-priced sales that are not genuine or comparable, the valuation challenge is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Solatium cannot be denied or differentiated solely because land was acquired under a different enactment when the government could apply the general land-acquisition provisions to that acquisition.
material_facts: The claimant sought solatium for land acquired under a state enactment.
That enactment empowered the government to apply provisions of the general land-acquisition law to the acquired land.
The Court relied on its recent decision holding that there was no justification for discriminating in solatium between acquisitions under different enactments.
The respondent did not controvert that position.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed payment of solatium on the compensation awarded by the High Court and otherwise confirmed the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3) of the Assam Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948, the government was empowered to apply provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, to acquired land. Relying on State of Kerala v. T.M. Peter, the Court held that there was no justification for discrimination in solatium between acquisitions under different enactments, particularly where such application was authorized.

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: An appeal concerns compensation for land acquired under a statutory acquisition framework.
predicates.solatium_claimed: The claimant seeks solatium in addition to compensation.
predicates.acquisition_framework_allows_general_lan: The framework for the acquisition permits the government to apply general land-acquisition provisions to the acquired land.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal involves a solatium claim and the acquisition framework allows general land-acquisition provisions to apply, solatium is payable on the compensation awarded.
